summary: Tarthang Tulku is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Tarthang Monastery and under teachers including Tarthang Choktrul, holding posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1962–1968) and the Nyingma Institute as Head Lama (~1972).

Tashi Densapa worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He served as editor for the Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1978, 2002) and as director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 2008).

Tashi Rabgey is a Tibetologist who studied at University College, Toronto, Magdalen College, Cambridge, and Harvard. She held posts at Georgetown University and the University of Virginia, where she was co-director of the Tibet Center.

Tashi Samphel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has served as director of the Songtsen Library (attested 2015) and as an associate professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Tashi Tsering is a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and history/archaeology. Educated at the Central School for Tibetans and under teachers including the 14th Dalai Lama, he held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (~1980–1992) and CIHTS.

Tatiana Oranskaia is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1968–1974) and Kendriya Hindi Sansthan. She held teaching posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1973–1998) and the University of Hamburg (1995–1996, 1998–2016).

Tatsugen Sato was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a doctorate at Komazawa University in 1978. He held academic appointments at Ryukoku University (attested 1974) and Komazawa University, serving as professor (attested 1994).
Tatsuo Hayashi was a philosopher who studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held posts at Hosei University (~1925–1932) as well as Toyo, Tsuda, Meiji, and Rikkyo Universities.

Tatsuo Nishida was a scholar of linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology who completed his doctorate at Kyoto University. He served as professor and dean at Kyoto University, president of the Linguistic Society of Japan (1979–1981), and professor at NACSIS (1992–1994).

Tavivat Puntarigvivat is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He held posts at Kyoto University, Mahidol University (attested 2005), and the World Buddhist University (attested 2013).
Taw Sein Ko was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Rangoon (~1880–1882), the Inner Temple, and the Inns of Court.

Teizo Iyanaga was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1940). He held faculty posts at Nagoya University (~1950–1968), the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976), and Sophia University (~1976–1983).

Tej Ram Sharma is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Banaras Hindu University in 1968 and held a post at Himachal Pradesh University (attested 1978).
Tendzin Chökyi Gyatso was an academic figure who studied under both the 14th Dalai Lama and Lobsang Gyatso, and also taught Lobsang Gyatso.

Tenga Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Benchen Monastery. He served as Dorje Lopön at Rumtek Monastery (~1967–1981) and later founded Benchen Monastery in 1976.

Tensei Kitabatake was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (-1955). He spent decades at Ryukoku University, ultimately serving as president (1995–1999), and later served as president of Gifu Shotoku Gakuen University (1999–2005).
Tenshin Tanouye was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied under Sogen Omori. He founded Chozen-ji and succeeded Sogen Omori.

Tenzin Dorjee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Geshe Sonam Rinchen, Geshe Dawa, and Geshe Lobsang Tsephel. He held posts at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and Pullahari Monastery (attested 2000).

Tenzin Namdak was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under sGangs ru Tshul khrims rgyal mtshan and earned a lha rams pa degree at Menri Monastery (1950–1953). He later founded Triten Norbutse Monastery in 1986.

Tenzin Norbu is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held a post at Columbia University and served as an assistant professor and department head at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).
